questions.question_text: Which protected class is covered by Wisconsin's Open Housing Law but NOT by the federal Fair Housing Act?
distractors: Race
Familial status
National origin
questions.explanation: Wis. Stat. s. 106.50 (1m) (nm) adds classes beyond the federal Fair Housing Act: sexual orientation, marital status, lawful source of income, age (18 and older), ancestry, and status as a victim of domestic abuse, sexual assault, or stalking. Race, familial status, and national origin are already federal classes.

questions.question_text: A landlord refuses to rent to an applicant who would pay with a federal Section 8 housing voucher. Under Wisconsin law, this is:
questions.correct_answer: Generally lawful — Wisconsin does not clearly treat vouchers as lawful source of income
distractors: Illegal discrimination based on lawful source of income
Illegal only in Milwaukee and Madison
Illegal only if the property has 5 or more units
questions.explanation: Wis. Stat. s. 106.50 protects 'lawful source of income' but never defines it. The annotation printed under the statute reads: 'Federal rent vouchers are not clearly within the meaning of lawful source of income. Knapp v. Eagle Property Management Corp., 54 F.3d 1272 (1995).' No Wisconsin statute requires a landlord to participate in the voluntary Section 8 program.

questions.question_text: A landlord refuses to rent to a 20-year-old applicant solely because of their age. Under the Open Housing Law, this is:
questions.correct_answer: Illegal, age 18 and older is a protected class
distractors: Legal, age is not protected in Wisconsin housing
Illegal only if the applicant is over 40
Legal unless the property receives federal funding
questions.explanation: Wisconsin's Open Housing Law protects age as a class, covering anyone 18 years old and older. This is broader than federal employment law (which protects only 40+) and applies statewide to housing.

questions.question_text: A property manager declines to show an apartment to a couple because they are unmarried. Under Wisconsin law, this is:
questions.correct_answer: Illegal discrimination based on marital status
distractors: Legal because marital status is not protected
Illegal only under federal fair housing law
Legal unless the property receives federal funding
questions.explanation: Marital status is a protected class under Wisconsin's Open Housing Law. Refusing to rent or show property based on whether someone is married, single, or divorced is illegal in Wisconsin.

questions.question_text: Under Wisconsin's Open Housing Law, what is the minimum age for the 'age' protected class?
distractors: 21 years old
40 years old
No minimum age
questions.explanation: Wisconsin's Open Housing Law protects age as a class, defined as 18 and older. This prevents discrimination against younger adults (18+) in housing, unlike federal employment law which protects those 40+.

questions.question_text: Which state agency enforces Wisconsin's Open Housing Law?
questions.correct_answer: The Equal Rights Division of the DWD
distractors: The Department of Safety and Professional Services
The Real Estate Examining Board
The Attorney General's Office
questions.explanation: Wisconsin's Open Housing Law is enforced by the Equal Rights Division within the Department of Workforce Development (DWD). Complaints can also be filed with HUD or pursued through private lawsuits.

questions.question_text: Within what timeframe must a housing discrimination complaint be filed with the Equal Rights Division?
distractors: 180 days after the alleged discrimination
6 months after the alleged discrimination
2 years after the alleged discrimination
questions.explanation: A person alleging a violation under Wisconsin's Open Housing Law must file a complaint with the Equal Rights Division within 1 year of the alleged discrimination. The federal HUD complaint deadline is also 1 year.

questions.question_text: A renter believes their landlord violated the Open Housing Law. Which is NOT a remedy option?
distractors: Filing a complaint with the Equal Rights Division
Filing a private lawsuit in state court
Filing a complaint with HUD
questions.explanation: Enforcement options include filing with the Equal Rights Division, filing with HUD, or pursuing a private lawsuit. Remedies include damages, injunctive relief, and attorney fees. Housing discrimination is typically a civil matter, not criminal.

questions.question_text: What remedies are available under Wisconsin's Open Housing Law?
questions.correct_answer: Damages, injunctive relief, and attorney fees
distractors: Only monetary damages up to $10,000
Only injunctive relief, no damages
Criminal penalties and imprisonment
questions.explanation: The Open Housing Law provides compensatory damages, injunctive relief, and attorney fees, and Wis. Stat. s. 106.50 (6) (h) authorizes forfeitures against a respondent found to have discriminated. Housing discrimination is a civil matter, not a criminal one.

questions.question_text: A person files a fair housing complaint with both the Equal Rights Division and HUD. Is this allowed?
questions.correct_answer: Yes, complaints may be filed with both agencies
distractors: No, only one agency at a time
Only if the complaint involves federal funds
Only for discrimination based on federal classes
questions.explanation: A complainant can file with the state Equal Rights Division and/or HUD and/or pursue a private lawsuit. Multiple avenues of enforcement are available and can be pursued simultaneously.

questions.question_text: A Wisconsin municipality wants to adopt its own fair housing ordinance. What may the ordinance do?
questions.correct_answer: Cover more types of housing than state law, using the state protected classes
distractors: Add protected classes that state law does not recognize
Set forfeitures lower than the state law amounts
Take effect only when a neighboring municipality adopts the same ordinance
questions.explanation: Wis. Stat. s. 66.1011 (2) lets political subdivisions prohibit housing discrimination 'solely on the basis of an individual being a member of a protected class,' and s. 66.1011 (1m) (d) defines that term by the state list in s. 106.50 (1m) (nm). The ordinance may be more inclusive as to the types of housing it covers, but its forfeitures may not be less than those in s. 106.50 (6) (h), and s. 66.1011 (3) forbids making it contingent on another municipality acting.

questions.question_text: A county ordinance bans housing discrimination against 'cohabitants,' a class not listed in Wis. Stat. s. 106.50. Is the ordinance valid?
questions.correct_answer: No, it exceeds the authority granted by s. 66.1011 (2)
distractors: Yes, counties may add any protected class they choose
Yes, but only in counties over 100,000 population
Yes, if the Equal Rights Division approves it first
questions.explanation: In County of Dane v. Norman, 174 Wis. 2d 683 (1993), the Wisconsin Supreme Court struck down exactly this provision. Wis. Stat. s. 66.1011 (2) authorizes local housing ordinances only as to members of a protected class as defined by state law in s. 106.50 (1m) (nm), so a locally invented class falls outside the grant of authority.

questions.question_text: A licensee intentionally discourages buyers from purchasing in a particular area on the basis of race. What penalty must the board impose for a first offense?
questions.correct_answer: Suspension of the license for at least 90 days
distractors: A written reprimand plus required fair housing education
Immediate revocation of the license
A $5,000 forfeiture with no suspension
questions.explanation: Wis. Stat. s. 452.14 (3) (jm) makes racial steering a ground for discipline, and s. 452.17 (4) (a) makes the penalty mandatory: the board shall suspend the license for not less than 90 days for a first offense and shall revoke it for a second. This is in addition to any penalty under s. 106.50 or s. 66.1011.

questions.question_text: A buyer asks a Wisconsin licensee about the racial makeup of a neighborhood. What does the license law require?
questions.correct_answer: The licensee may not disclose the information
distractors: The licensee must answer truthfully if they know
The licensee must refer the buyer to the Equal Rights Division
The licensee may answer if the buyer puts the request in writing
questions.explanation: Wis. Stat. s. 452.23 (1) bars a licensee from disclosing, in connection with a sale, exchange, purchase, or rental of real property, information whose disclosure would itself constitute unlawful discrimination in housing under s. 106.50 or handicap discrimination under federal law. Answering the question would be the violation.

questions.question_text: Beyond a complaint to the Equal Rights Division, what additional exposure does a Wisconsin licensee face for a fair housing violation?
questions.correct_answer: Separate discipline by the Real Estate Examining Board
distractors: Automatic criminal prosecution by the district attorney
A mandatory civil judgment for triple damages
Suspension of the firm's license in every state where it operates
questions.explanation: Wis. Stat. s. 452.14 (3) (n) makes it a ground for discipline to treat any person unequally solely because of sex, race, color, handicap, national origin, ancestry, marital status, lawful source of income, or status as a victim of domestic abuse, sexual assault, or stalking. Board discipline runs alongside, not instead of, the s. 106.50 remedies.
